card.statement:
The Jordan--Schwinger map for a matrix $X=(X_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$ is defined as follows <<cite:BidernharnLouck1981>>:

\begin{equation}
X\mapsto \sum\limits_{i,j=1}^n X_{ij} a_i a_j^{*},
\end{equation}

where $\{a_i, a_j^*\}_{i,j=1}^n$ are boson creation and annihilation operators, i.e. the elements of the canonical commutation relations (CCR) algebra. Hence <<ref:def:DA>> can be described using Jordan--Schwinger maps. For that, instead of general elements of the CCR algebra, consider their realizations by operators of multiplication and derivation to underline the linearity of operators. Furthermore, if we set $V=W=\mathbb{R}^n$ in the definition of <<ref:def:DA>> then <<ref:def:DX>> in our notation is given by

\[
X\mapsto D(X^*).
\]

Consequently, as the following Lemma <<ref:lem:CommRelations>> shows, <<ref:def:DA>> defines an anti-homomorphism, while <<ref:def:DX>> gives a homomorphism.
card.label: Remark 5

paper.title: Convex topological algebras via linear vector fields and Cuntz algebras
paper.abstract: Realization by linear vector fields is constructed for any Lie algebra which admits a biorthogonal system and for its any suitable representation. The embedding into Lie algebras of linear vector fields is analogous to the classical Jordan-Schwinger map. A number of examples of such Lie algebras of linear vector fields is computed. In particular, we obtain examples of the twisted Heisenberg-Virasoro Lie algebra and the Schrödinger-Virasoro Lie algebras among others. More generally, we construct an embedding of an arbitrary locally convex topological algebra into the Cuntz algebra.
